Natural Chaos is an abstract strategy game where each player controls two natural elements. The goal is to get four of your elements in a row on one of the four playing boards. But watch out the elements have a four way rock paper scissors type ranking system that allows you to keep your opponent on their toes! [Rating: 4/10] Playing across 4 boards was unintuitive. Game just kinda ends abruptly when you lose track of one pattern or another and your opponent takes advantage. Otherwise you just do your best to block each other.

[Rating: 5/10] Abstract game with 4-in a row as core, but with elements where each player has 2 natural elements, and they interact with each other. Idea is neat, but for me it is forgettable.

[Rating: 5/10] why a 5? the game itself works but it's not extremely exciting, I'd say. On the contrary, its developement is rather slow. The real problem for me though, it's that there is nothing to prevent this game to drag on forever (like, for instance, Hive). There are abstract games in which, try as you might, you can't play forever, you cannot sabotage a game... such as Dvonn, Tzaar and so on. (I know of games with this feature that I still like, such as Octi, but here the problem compounds with the slow rhythm) I'll try again to see if I can change my mind
